back_translation: Then he brought me into the main hall and measured the jambs to be six cubits wide on each side.
The width of the entrance was ten cubits, and the side walls of the entrance were five cubits on each side. He measured the length of the main hall to be forty cubits and its width twenty cubits.
Then he went inside and measured the jambs of the entrance to be two cubits wide; the entrance was six cubits wide, and the side walls of the entrance were seven cubits wide on each side.
He measured the room adjoining the main hall to be twenty cubits long and twenty cubits wide, and he said to me, 'This is the Most Holy Place.'
Then he measured the wall of the temple to be six cubits thick, and each side room around the temple was four cubits wide.

The side rooms were in three stories, thirty rooms to each story. On the temple wall all around there were ledges projecting out to support the side rooms, so that the beams would not be fastened into the temple wall itself.

The side rooms grew wider as they rose higher, because the structure surrounding the temple ascended in stages all around the temple; so the rooms widened as they rose, and a winding stairway went up from the lowest story through the middle to the highest.
I saw that the temple had a raised base all around, the foundation of the side rooms, a full rod high—six long cubits.
The outer wall of the side rooms was five cubits thick, and the open space between the side rooms of the temple
and the outer chambers was twenty cubits wide all around the temple.
The side rooms opened onto that space, with one entrance on the north and another on the south; and that space was five cubits wide all around.
The building facing the open area behind the temple on the west was seventy cubits wide; the wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, and its length was ninety cubits.
Then he measured the temple to be a hundred cubits long, and the open area together with the building and its walls was also a hundred cubits long.
The width of the front of the temple together with the open area on the east was a hundred cubits.

Then he measured the length of the building facing the open area behind the temple, including its galleries on each side; it was a hundred cubits. As for the main hall, the inner room, and the porticoes facing the court,

that is, the thresholds, the beveled windows, and the galleries on three sides all around opposite the threshold—all were paneled with wood from the floor up to the windows, and the windows were covered.
Above the entrance, both inside and outside the temple, and on every wall all around, both inside and outside, there were decorations according to the measured pattern.
Carved cherubim and palm trees were set alternately, a palm tree between each pair of cherubim, and each cherub had two faces:

one face, the face of a man, turned toward the palm tree on one side, and the other, the face of a young lion, turned toward the palm tree on the other side. They were carved like this all around the temple.
From the floor to above the entrance, cherubim and palm trees were carved on the wall of the main hall.
The main hall had a rectangular doorframe, and the front of the Most Holy Place had a similar appearance.
There was a wooden altar three cubits high and two cubits long; its corners, base, and sides were of wood. And he said to me, 'This is the table that is before the LORD.'
Both the main hall and the Most Holy Place had double doors,
and each door had two folding panels—two panels for one door and two for the other.
On the doors of the main hall, cherubim and palm trees were carved like those on the walls, and there was a wooden canopy outside, in front of the portico.
On the side walls of the portico, on both sides, were beveled windows and palm trees. The side rooms of the temple also had canopies.
